title: A done bug whose check or repro names a deleted test fails the review's rerun with no route out
goal: A sprint review whose done items carry a check or bug repro naming a test that a later change deleted (a -k selection that collects nothing, exit 5) has a route to finish, as gate dead-test settles, and SP-eahtellz's seven such bugs (BG-2luo4b26, BG-co3nthy4, BG-hway4bjs, BG-kc7uzged, BG-kjpbqany, BG-mnnihwaf, BG-r5fab2td) take it, so ST-lpazcjki's done passes; today set refuses to clear a repro and refuses a repro that passes, and reopen leaves the bug unable to pass done. Found in the SP-eahtellz review.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_base,bl_land;bl=bl_base.Backlog('.');bl.sprint_items=lambda s:['BG-2luo4b26'];r=bl_land.rerun_done_checks(bl,'SP-eahtellz');print('failing reruns',[(i,c) for i,_,c in r]);sys.exit(1 if r else 0)

gates.question: How should a done item's check or repro that names a deleted test (its -k collects nothing, exit 5) be handled at the review's rerun?
options: skip-gone: rerun_done_checks reports such a check or repro as gone (a warning naming the item and the selector), not a failure; the items stay as they are, and a new item's done still refuses a selection that collects nothing
retire: set --check and --repro on a done item accept a replacement with a reason naming the deleted test, without reopening it; the seven bugs get python3 _tools/tests.py
